data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 and SRC_003 share a mechanism — the topological observation that removing a 1-dimensional set (zero-width cut lines) from a 2-dimensional connected open set leaves it path-connected — and therefore reduce to the same underlying claim of a single piece. They are REFUTED IF their counterconditions reveal a structural difference rather than merely a different emphasis: SRC_001 frames the manifold-level argument and lists combinatorial and kerf counterconditions, while SRC_003 frames the same argument as a measure-theoretic/topological one with closure and closed-disk counterconditions. If both countercondition sets collapse to the same two rivals (combinatorial counting and physical kerf), the candidates are equivalent; if SRC_003's closure/disk cases produce a genuinely different remainder structure, they do not reduce.
